Race conditions like this are tough to debug from CI logs alone. If you'd like to automate the triage, FixSense is a free GitHub Action that analyzes failing Playwright tests with AI — gives you root cause, flakiness score (0-100), and whether it's an app bug or test timing issue.

```yaml
- name: FixSense Analysis
  if: failure()
  uses: CopilotMe/fixsense-action@v1
  with:
    api-key: ${{ secrets.FIXSENSE_API_KEY }}
```

Free plan: 350 analyses/month. Could help quantify how flaky this is across runs without manually checking each one.

Also: realized that OPENCODE_CHANNEL also changes the database name and would be a breaking change to change it. Nixpkgs sets it to "stable", this repo package sets it to "local", arch leaves it unset (seems to default to "dev" in most cases) github releases sets it to "prod"/"beta" and all other distributions seem to be binary distributions pulling github releases

need to seek guidance on best option since setting the channel has consequeces beyond database name as well (icon/bundle name for desktop app on macos) - its kind of a weird spot since nix users can pin a tag and get the same build as a release (most similar to prod) or pin to a branch (beta or dev) but the derivation isn't aware

Leaning towards making it "dev" (removing setting OPENCODE_CHANNEL)

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #20751: [FEATURE]: Add debug capabilities for opencode github action — both request better visibility/debugging output for the GitHub Action runner (console/log output of agent decisions and execution flow)

This is close to #20751, but the request here is narrower and more specific.

I am asking for structured GitHub-action-visible execution metadata, not just more debug output in general. The main gaps are:
- selected flow
- prompt source
- branch outcome
- summary fallback vs normal response
- PR creation/reuse/skip reason
- tool timing

If maintainers prefer, I am happy to fold this into #20751 instead of keeping a separate issue.

Adding a more concrete scope here.

The most useful GitHub Action debug data would be:
- selected flow: issue, PR, fork PR, schedule, workflow_dispatch
- prompt source: trigger comment, default review prompt, custom PROMPT input
- branch outcome: checked out branch, branch switched during run, dirty/uncommitted/head-changed result
- response path: normal assistant text vs fallback summary
- PR outcome: created, reused existing PR, or skipped, with the reason
- tool execution timing: at least start/end or duration

This would make GitHub runs much easier to debug without having to infer behavior from partial logs.

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #19284: Reports the same root cause — external/custom `messageID` causes `lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id` to fail, resulting in extra assistant turns and a runaway loop.
- #17982: Reports the prompt loop continuing after `finish=stop` due to the same ID comparison logic in `session/prompt.ts`, causing invalid continuation calls that end with an assistant-last transcript.

Both issues trace back to the same code paths in `session/prompt.ts` that compare opaque message IDs for ordering. It may be worth coordinating with or closing in favor of those issues.

> This isn't a bug it is intentional behavior the prompt history from the tui frontend is shared everywhere but it doesn't affect your agents or the history of the session, this "prompt history" is just the last 50 or so inputs you sent and it is global.

Recommend re-evaluating this position as it is counterintuitive, and others are stepping on this and reporting issues and even a PR to 'fix' it. I just ran into this by running the last prompt in the wrong session. A new session should not have any prompt history, and other project sessions should have their histories tied to their respective sessions. I can't think of any good reason for them to cross over, especially given that two live sessions in separate project folders are not live-updating the opposite's history, so we run into a similar issue as when overlapping bash histories overwrite themselves based on the last session to close. This makes no sense in the context of a tool which has per-project sessions - such division should not end at the prompt history.
